whatIsSection.title: What Is
whatIsSection.subtitle: Sensitive teeth treatment focuses on reducing pain caused by exposed dentin or irritated tooth nerves. Sensitivity commonly occurs when enamel wears down or gums recede, exposing the inner layers of the tooth.

whyMattersBox.title: Common Causes at a Glance
whyMattersBox.paragraph: Tooth sensitivity can stem from several underlying issues. Identifying the exact cause is the first step toward lasting relief.

items.title: Enamel Erosion
items.description: Worn enamel exposes the sensitive dentin layer underneath, leading to sharp pain with hot or cold foods.

items.title: Gum Recession
items.description: Receding gums expose tooth roots that are not protected by enamel, causing heightened sensitivity.

items.title: Cavities & Worn Fillings
items.description: Untreated cavities or aging fillings can allow temperature and pressure to reach the tooth's nerve.

items.title: Teeth Grinding
items.description: Chronic grinding wears down enamel over time, gradually increasing sensitivity.

items.question: What causes tooth sensitivity?
items.answer: Common causes include enamel erosion, gum recession, cavities, worn fillings, cracked teeth, teeth grinding, and gum disease.

items.question: Is tooth sensitivity permanent?
items.answer: Not always. In many cases, professional treatment and proper oral care can significantly reduce or eliminate sensitivity.

items.question: How is sensitive teeth treatment performed?
items.answer: Treatment depends on the cause and may include fluoride applications, desensitizing agents, dental bonding, fillings, gum treatment, or restorative procedures.

items.question: Can sensitive teeth be prevented?
items.answer: Yes. Good oral hygiene, using a soft-bristled toothbrush, avoiding excessive acidic foods, and regular dental check-ups help prevent sensitivity.

items.question: How much does sensitive teeth treatment cost in Pune?
items.answer: The cost varies depending on the cause of sensitivity and the treatment required. A consultation allows your dentist to provide an accurate estimate.

items.question: When should I see a dentist for sensitive teeth?
items.answer: If sensitivity lasts for several days, worsens over time, or interferes with eating and drinking, you should schedule a dental examination promptly.
